findings.summary: Nothing pins that the pod KEEPS its term after a non-Fenced IOException -- the mutation local.close(); local = null; before letting the ambiguous failure escape FleetSequencer.commitAll leaves every test green.
findings.failure_scenario: Mutate the commit path so any IOException, not only FencedException, demotes the pod. anAMBIGUOUSLocalFailureIsPROPAGATED_NeverForwarded still passes -- it asserts only that an IOException carrying "the reply was lost" escapes, that transport.sentTo() is empty and that deltasCarrying(store, "seg/b") is zero, and it never re-reads mine.leading() after the throw. The other five tests never drive a non-Fenced local failure at all. In production that mutation means a leaseholder that hits one transient 503 on its delta PUT silently drops its LocalSequencer while the lease object still names it: leading() flips to false so the pod unpublishes its own endpoint, and its next commit re-elects -- burning an epoch and paying a fresh seal plus a full chain recover() for a store hiccup that LocalSequencer.renewForever deliberately refuses to fail over on. Adding assertThat(mine.leading()).isTrue() after the assertThatThrownBy kills it.

findings.summary: Deleting local.close() from the FencedException branch survives the whole suite -- no assertion observes that the fenced local sequencer is shut down.
findings.failure_scenario: Make the close a no-op (keep local = null). aLeaderThatIsFENCEDFallsBackToForwardingRatherThanFailing still passes: the offset assertion, first.leading() false and deltasCarrying(store, "seg/b") == 1 all hold, and first.close() at the end takes the local == null path so it observes nothing either. The Refusing fake even carries a closed field that no assertion ever reads. The behaviour that goes unchecked is real: in that test the fence arrives from CommitLog's seal discovery, not from the renewer, so poda's LocalSequencer.fenced is never latched and its renewer thread is still parked on its tick -- with the close dropped it wakes and spends a stat, a get and a losing putIfMatch renewing a term podc already holds, and the LocalSequencer plus its LeaseManager belief are leaked once per fencing, all with the build green.
